metaTitle: Drywall Hole Repair in Santa Monica, CA | Tarea
metaDescription: Fix a punched or cracked drywall hole in Santa Monica for $200–$365. Learn common causes, what a pro does, and when to call one.
intro: A hole in your drywall in Santa Monica can start small—a doorknob dent, a moving-day scrape—but it tends to grow if the edges crumble or moisture gets into the paper backing. Coastal humidity here softens drywall paper faster than in drier inland areas, so a patch that would hold up elsewhere can fail sooner near the beach.
causes: A door swung too hard and the knob punched through the wall, often because a corroded or loose doorstop no longer catches it.
Furniture or luggage bumped a corner, cracking the drywall's paper face.
Salt-laden coastal air has corroded a hinge or closer, letting a door slam into the wall repeatedly until it broke through.
Moisture from ocean humidity softened the drywall paper over time, so a minor bump tore a bigger hole than it would have inland.
An old patch job used the wrong material or was never sanded flush, and it eventually cracked and fell out.
whatProDoes: Cuts away loose or damaged drywall around the hole to reach solid material.
Installs a backing piece or patch (mesh tape for small holes, a scrap drywall piece screwed to furring strips for larger ones).
Applies joint compound in thin layers, letting each dry and sanding between coats for a flush surface.
Primes and, if requested, paints the patched area to match the surrounding wall.
Checks nearby door hardware or hinges if that's what caused the damage, so the same spot doesn't get hit again.
diyOrPro: A small nail hole or minor dent is fine to patch yourself with spackle from a hardware store. Anything larger than a fist, anywhere near electrical wiring or plumbing behind the wall, or in a spot with visible water staining should go to a pro, since cutting into a wall blind can hit wiring or reveal hidden moisture damage that needs more than a patch.
priceNote: In Santa Monica this job runs $200 to $365, based on an $83 hourly rate for a typical 2 to 4 hour visit. The time depends mostly on hole size and how many coats of compound and sanding passes are needed to get an invisible finish, plus whether paint-matching is part of the job.

faqs.q: Will the patch be invisible once it's painted?
faqs.a: A properly sanded and primed patch should blend in closely, but exact color match depends on your existing paint's age and sheen, which can fade differently near the coast.

faqs.q: Why did my drywall hole happen in the first place?
faqs.a: Often it's a door that swings too far because a doorstop or hinge has corroded from salt air, but it can also be simple impact damage from furniture or daily bumps.

faqs.q: Can the pro also fix the door that caused the hole?
faqs.a: They can look at the hinge or doorstop while on site, but hardware replacement is a separate job from the drywall repair itself and would be quoted separately.
